annotations.description:
Runner cache volume saves are failing on {{ $labels.platform }}: {{ $values.A.Value | humanizePercentage }} of the jobs that saved a volume in the last hour (at least 20) had their save refused (invalid_image, incomplete, error or timeout). A refused save keeps the previous copy, so the next jobs start from stale or empty caches and the loss compounds until the cause is fixed. Unchanged, withheld and release_pending saves are excluded because they are not failures.

First query (Pulse SQL, the pulse-sql data source): SELECT CASE WHEN json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'job') = 'tuist-macos-tart-kubelet' THEN 'macos' ELSE 'linux' END AS platform, regexp_match(body, '"result":"([^"]*)"')[1] AS result, regexp_match(body, '"kind":"([^"]*)"')[1] AS kind, count(*) AS n FROM opentelemetry_logs WHERE timestamp > now() - INTERVAL '1 hour' AND json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'cluster') = 'tuist-production' AND body LIKE '%"operation":"publish"%' AND (json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'job') = 'tuist-macos-tart-kubelet' AND body LIKE '%"msg":"cache phase"%' OR json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'namespace') = 'tuist-runners' AND json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'service_name') = 'agent' AND body LIKE '%"msg":"cache volume operation"%') GROUP BY platform, result, kind. Then read the error field of a few failing lines: select body with the same filter plus AND body LIKE '%"result":"invalid_image"%' (or the failing result), ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 20.

Likely causes:
- macOS invalid_image "cache image failed write-back verification": the guest could not open or write its image through the VM share. Check whether a runner image or tart-kubelet release went out just before the onset (on 2026-10-21 runner image 0.43.1 refused every save from 17:00 to 20:37).
- macOS incomplete: the image holds less than the guest wrote (lost guest writes). See the incomplete rule.
- Linux invalid_image with a maintenance "loop device still has live references" error: the agent verified a volume kubelet still held and poisoned the save (2026-10-20 to 10-22, fixed by #14590).
- error "image upload failed": the cache upload endpoint or Kura is failing.

Roll back the release that started it; there is no per-account mitigation.
annotations.summary: {{ $values.A.Value | humanizePercentage }} of {{ $labels.platform }} runner cache volume saves failed in the last hour

model.rawSql:
SELECT platform, CASE WHEN saves >= 20 THEN CAST(failed AS DOUBLE) / saves ELSE 0 END AS value
FROM (
  SELECT platform, count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN result IN ('invalid_image', 'incomplete', 'error', 'timeout') THEN use END) AS failed, count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN result NOT IN ('unchanged', 'withheld', 'release_pending', 'cancelled') THEN use END) AS saves
  FROM (
    SELECT CASE WHEN json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'job') = 'tuist-macos-tart-kubelet' THEN 'macos' ELSE 'linux' END AS platform, COALESCE(regexp_match(body, '"result":"([^"]*)"')[1], '') AS result, COALESCE(regexp_match(body, '"use":"([^"]*)"')[1], '') AS use
    FROM opentelemetry_logs
    WHERE timestamp > now() - INTERVAL '1 hour'
      AND ((json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'job') = 'tuist-macos-tart-kubelet' AND json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'env') = 'production') AND body LIKE '%"msg":"cache phase"%' OR (json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'cluster') = 'tuist-production' AND json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'namespace') = 'tuist-runners' AND json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'service_name') = 'agent') AND body LIKE '%"msg":"cache volume operation"%')
      AND body LIKE '%"operation":"publish"%'
  ) l
  GROUP BY platform
) s

annotations.description:
Jobs on {{ $labels.platform }} are starting without their cache volume: {{ $values.C.Value | humanizePercentage }} of {{ $values.B.Value }} volume attaches in the last hour were refused or failed, so those jobs ran cold. GitHub binding delays (execution_pending) are excluded and alert separately.

First query (Pulse SQL, the pulse-sql data source): SELECT CASE WHEN json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'job') = 'tuist-macos-tart-kubelet' THEN 'macos' ELSE 'linux' END AS platform, regexp_match(body, '"result":"([^"]*)"')[1] AS result, count(*) AS n FROM opentelemetry_logs WHERE timestamp > now() - INTERVAL '1 hour' AND json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'cluster') = 'tuist-production' AND (json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'job') = 'tuist-macos-tart-kubelet' AND regexp_like(body, '"msg":"(cache phase","operation":"attach"|custom cache volume)') OR json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'namespace') = 'tuist-runners' AND json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'service_name') = 'agent' AND body LIKE '%"operation":"acquire"%') GROUP BY platform, result, then read the msg and error of the refusals by selecting body with the same filter plus AND body NOT LIKE '%"result":"success"%'. The guest sees it as `Cache volume unavailable: <reason>` in the runner log.

Likely causes:
- macOS capacity, "custom cache volume unavailable; job continues cold ... cache capacity exhausted": the host has no room for the volume. Check host disk (tuist_runner_cache_volume_filesystem_available_bytes) and whether admission reserves more than volumes need.
- macOS "custom cache volume larger than this host holds": the server answered 507 because the lineage's capacity exceeds the host maximum.
- Linux timeout: the agent did not attach within its 25 second acquire budget, typically because it waited on a download, and the guest got `cache service returned 503`.
- error or "not authorized": the server refused allocation; check the server logs for the runner cache volumes controller.
annotations.summary: {{ $values.C.Value | humanizePercentage }} of {{ $labels.platform }} runner cache volume attaches failed in the last hour ({{ $values.B.Value }} attaches)

model.rawSql:
SELECT platform, sum(CASE WHEN platform = 'macos' AND result NOT IN ('success', 'cancelled') OR platform = 'linux' AND result NOT IN ('success', 'cancelled', 'execution_pending') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS value
FROM (
  SELECT CASE WHEN json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'job') = 'tuist-macos-tart-kubelet' THEN 'macos' ELSE 'linux' END AS platform, COALESCE(regexp_match(body, '"result":"([^"]*)"')[1], '') AS result, COALESCE(regexp_match(body, '"use":"([^"]*)"')[1], '') AS use
  FROM opentelemetry_logs
  WHERE timestamp > now() - INTERVAL '1 hour'
    AND ((json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'job') = 'tuist-macos-tart-kubelet' AND json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'env') = 'production') AND regexp_like(body, '"msg":"(cache phase","operation":"attach"|custom cache volume (not authorized;|larger than this host))') OR (json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'cluster') = 'tuist-production' AND json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'namespace') = 'tuist-runners' AND json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'service_name') = 'agent') AND body LIKE '%"msg":"cache volume operation"%' AND body LIKE '%"operation":"acquire"%')
) l
GROUP BY platform

SELECT platform, sum(CASE WHEN platform = 'macos' AND result <> 'cancelled' OR platform = 'linux' AND result NOT IN ('cancelled', 'execution_pending') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS value
FROM (
  SELECT CASE WHEN json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'job') = 'tuist-macos-tart-kubelet' THEN 'macos' ELSE 'linux' END AS platform, COALESCE(regexp_match(body, '"result":"([^"]*)"')[1], '') AS result, COALESCE(regexp_match(body, '"use":"([^"]*)"')[1], '') AS use
  FROM opentelemetry_logs
  WHERE timestamp > now() - INTERVAL '1 hour'
    AND ((json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'job') = 'tuist-macos-tart-kubelet' AND json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'env') = 'production') AND regexp_like(body, '"msg":"(cache phase","operation":"attach"|custom cache volume (not authorized;|larger than this host))') OR (json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'cluster') = 'tuist-production' AND json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'namespace') = 'tuist-runners' AND json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'service_name') = 'agent') AND body LIKE '%"msg":"cache volume operation"%' AND body LIKE '%"operation":"acquire"%')
) l
GROUP BY platform

annotations.description:
{{ $values.A.Value }} runner cache volume and checkout attaches in the last 30 minutes were refused with execution_pending: the server could not tell which GitHub job each runner is running, so it would not scope a volume and those jobs ran cold. The binding comes from GitHub's workflow_job in_progress webhook, with ExecutionLookupWorker reading the GitHub API as a fallback. Baseline is 0 to 2 per 30 minutes; a burst means GitHub is delivering in_progress late (and its API reports the job late too).

Check https://www.githubstatus.com for degraded Webhooks or Actions first. There is nothing to fix on our side when GitHub is delayed; jobs keep running, only without their caches.

First query (Pulse SQL, the pulse-sql data source): SELECT count(*) FROM opentelemetry_logs WHERE timestamp > now() - INTERVAL '1 hour' AND json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'cluster') = 'tuist-production' AND json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'service_name') = 'tuist' AND body LIKE '%execution lookup found no job%' (normally about 5 per hour; 1,237 per hour on 2026-10-21). The host side is the same table with json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'namespace') = 'tuist-runners' AND json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'service_name') = 'agent' AND body LIKE '%execution_pending%' for Linux and json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'job') = 'tuist-macos-tart-kubelet' AND body LIKE '%not authorized in time%' for macOS.

Likely causes:
- GitHub webhook delivery delays (2026-10-21 14:52 to 19:23 UTC).
- Our webhook endpoint is failing or slow: check the GitHub App's recent deliveries and the :webhooks Oban queue.
- The GitHub App installation lost access, so the API fallback fails too: look for `execution lookup failed to list jobs` in the server logs.
annotations.summary: {{ $values.A.Value }} runner cache volume attaches waited on a GitHub job binding in the last 30 minutes

model.rawSql:
SELECT count(*) AS value
FROM opentelemetry_logs
WHERE timestamp > now() - INTERVAL '30 minutes'
  AND ((json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'cluster') = 'tuist-production' AND json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'namespace') = 'tuist-runners' AND json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'service_name') = 'agent') AND body LIKE '%"msg":"cache volume operation"%' AND body LIKE '%"result":"execution_pending"%' AND regexp_like(body, '"operation":"(acquire|checkout_acquire)"') OR (json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'job') = 'tuist-macos-tart-kubelet' AND json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'env') = 'production') AND regexp_like(body, '"msg":"(custom cache volume not authorized in time|[^"]*execution_pending)'))

title: Runner cache volumes waiting on GitHub job binding

annotations.description:
Only {{ $values.C.Value | humanizePercentage }} of the {{ $values.B.Value }} {{ $labels.platform }} cache volume uses attached in the last two hours whose lineage had a saved copy started warm; the rest attached cold. Read from Postgres (runner_cache_volume_uses.warm with base_generation > 0), excluding the e2e-reuse-* keys, the runners-acceptance-probe key and checkout volumes. The normal minimum from 2026-10-17 to 10-22 was 86% on macOS and 95% on Linux. Cold starts are slower builds, and a cold job's save is withheld so it cannot replace a good head.

First query (Pulse SQL, the pulse-sql data source), macOS: SELECT json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'instance') AS instance, regexp_match(body, '"source":"([^"]*)"')[1] AS source, count(*) AS n FROM opentelemetry_logs WHERE timestamp > now() - INTERVAL '2 hours' AND json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'job') = 'tuist-macos-tart-kubelet' AND json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'env') = 'production' AND body LIKE '%"msg":"cache phase"%' AND body LIKE '%"operation":"attach"%' AND body LIKE '%"result":"success"%' AND body NOT LIKE '%"kind":"checkout"%' GROUP BY instance, source to see whether the cold attaches (source cold) concentrate on some hosts. Per account, query runner_cache_volume_uses joined to runner_cache_volumes on the ops read-only role (the Grafana role cannot read account_id).

Likely causes:
- Masters evicted on the hosts jobs land on: look for `"operation":"evict"` and host disk pressure.
- Placement sends an account's jobs to hosts that hold none of its masters (a new rack host per job, or a fleet change).
- Prefetch is not keeping up: `"operation":"prefetch"` with result capacity or timeout.
annotations.summary: Only {{ $values.C.Value | humanizePercentage }} of {{ $labels.platform }} cache volume uses with a saved copy started warm in the last 2 hours ({{ $values.B.Value }} uses)

model.rawSql: SELECT v.platform AS platform, count(*) FILTER (WHERE u.warm) AS value FROM runner_cache_volume_uses u JOIN runner_cache_volumes v ON v.id = u.volume_id WHERE u.attached_at >= now() - interval '2 hours' AND u.base_generation > 0 AND u.warm IS NOT NULL AND v.key NOT LIKE 'e2e-reuse-%' AND v.key NOT IN ('runners-acceptance-probe', 'checkout') GROUP BY v.platform

SELECT v.platform AS platform, count(*) AS value FROM runner_cache_volume_uses u JOIN runner_cache_volumes v ON v.id = u.volume_id WHERE u.attached_at >= now() - interval '2 hours' AND u.base_generation > 0 AND u.warm IS NOT NULL AND v.key NOT LIKE 'e2e-reuse-%' AND v.key NOT IN ('runners-acceptance-probe', 'checkout') GROUP BY v.platform

title: Runner cache volume warm rate low

annotations.description:
{{ $values.A.Value }} macOS cache volume saves in the last hour were withheld as incomplete: the image the host read back holds fewer bytes than the guest reported writing, so the guest's last writes never reached it. Publishing it would have restored an empty or partial volume to the next job, so the host withholds it and the previous copy stays. One is enough to look at: on a healthy fleet there are none.

First query (Pulse SQL, the pulse-sql data source): SELECT timestamp, json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'instance') AS instance, body FROM opentelemetry_logs WHERE timestamp > now() - INTERVAL '1 hour' AND json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'job') = 'tuist-macos-tart-kubelet' AND json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'env') = 'production' AND body LIKE '%"msg":"cache phase"%' AND body LIKE '%"result":"incomplete"%' ORDER BY timestamp DESC, which names the instance (host), and the pod, scope and byte counts in error.

Likely causes:
- The guest's writes did not reach the image before the VM stopped (an unclean guest shutdown or a lost APFS checkpoint).
- A runner image or tart-kubelet change in how the image is shared with the guest or flushed at job end. Check what was released before the first one.
- One host's disk or APFS container misbehaving: several on the same instance point at the host.
annotations.summary: {{ $values.A.Value }} macOS cache volume saves lost guest writes in the last hour

model.rawSql:
SELECT count(*) AS value
FROM opentelemetry_logs
WHERE timestamp > now() - INTERVAL '1 hour'
  AND (json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'job') = 'tuist-macos-tart-kubelet' AND json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'env') = 'production')
  AND body LIKE '%"msg":"cache phase"%'
  AND body LIKE '%"operation":"publish"%'
  AND body LIKE '%"result":"incomplete"%'

annotations.description:
{{ $values.A.Value }} times in the last 30 minutes a GitHub Actions OIDC token a job minted named a different job for its runner than GitHub's workflow_job in_progress webhook or jobs API did. The token binds the runner session at job start and its claims scope the job's cache volumes, so a disagreement means one source is wrong, which should never happen. The later binding replaces the token's and allocation stops using the token's claims, so the job falls back to GitHub's binding.

First query (Pulse SQL, the pulse-sql data source): SELECT timestamp, body FROM opentelemetry_logs WHERE timestamp > now() - INTERVAL '1 hour' AND json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'cluster') = 'tuist-production' AND json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'service_name') = 'tuist' AND body LIKE '%execution token disagrees with the recorded execution%' ORDER BY timestamp DESC. Each line carries runner_name, workflow_job_id (the token's job) and recorded_workflow_job_id (the other source's). Compare both jobs' repository and run in runner_workflow_jobs and the session in runner_sessions.

Likely causes:
- check_run_id is not the workflow job id for some job kind (reusable workflows, matrix jobs).
- A runner name collision within the account.
- A token replayed from another job of the same repository.
annotations.summary: {{ $values.A.Value }} runner execution tokens disagreed with GitHub's job binding in the last 30 minutes

model.rawSql:
SELECT count(*) AS value
FROM opentelemetry_logs
WHERE timestamp > now() - INTERVAL '30 minutes'
  AND json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'cluster') = 'tuist-production'
  AND json_get_string(resource_attributes, 'service_name') = 'tuist'
  AND body LIKE '%execution token disagrees with the recorded execution%'

title: Runner execution token disagrees with GitHub
